articles.title: NEW YORK FEDERAL JUDGE DENIES NOVIG'S INJUNCTION BID
articles.summary: Judge Colleen McMahon denied the preliminary injunction Novig sought against New York, finding that its sports event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act because they don't depend on events with a financial or economic consequence, and “bear more than a passing resemblance to sports betting.” That lets the state require Novig to get a gambling license or stop listing sports contracts. Novig's operator, Ludlow Exchange, got CFTC contract market designation in June, began serving New York customers in August, and sued Attorney General Letitia James on August 5, arguing federal preemption. The ruling follows a similar denial for Kalshi earlier this year, and lawyer Daniel Wallach says all 10 Second Circuit federal rulings in sports prediction-market cases have favored the states, with state regulators possibly moving to enforcement in state court.

articles.title: ALTA: AIRWALLEX CO-FOUNDER TO BUILD ONCHAIN FINANCE INFRASTRUCTURE
articles.summary: Alta, operated by Nexus Networks, raised to build onchain finance infrastructure spanning cross-border payments, embedded finance, treasury management, and compliance controls. Founder Loong Wang frames the addressable problem as $4T in trapped cash, $1.4T in counterparty risk, and $135B in operational waste in global corporate finance. The treasury product combines FX conversion at settlement with onchain yield through tokenized money market funds, while the compliance layer applies policy controls at the transaction level across all product areas. A fourth vertical targets agentic commerce, building payment rails for AI agents that transact autonomously.

articles.title: VISA ADDS MONAD TO STABLECOIN SETTLEMENT NETWORK
articles.summary: Visa added Monad as a stablecoin settlement option for participating issuers and acquirers, bringing its blockchain settlement network to 10 chains that also include Ethereum, Solana, Base, Polygon, Avalanche, Stellar, Canton, Tempo, and Circle's Arc. The program reached a $20 billion annualized settlement run rate as of September, up 15x year over year, with 225 stablecoin-linked card programs live globally. Monad is building an institutional privacy feature, expected in the coming months, that keeps transaction details confidential from public view while remaining auditable by regulators and sharing liquidity with the public chain. The network's ability to settle on weekends and holidays distinguishes it from traditional card rails, which operate on a five-business-day banking schedule.

articles.title: BUILDING A TOKENIZED SECURITIES VENUE ON UNISWAP
articles.summary: The SEC's September 2026 Innovation Exemption established Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs), a new venue category permitting AMMs on public blockchains to trade tokenized NMS stocks without registering as exchanges or ATSs, with compliant liquidity providers exempt from dealer registration. Uniswap has processed over $20 billion in stock token volume to date, with Robinhood Chain generating $900 million across 130,000 wallets in three months through 40+ SPY-paired pools. TSV compliance requires KYL and KYC identity gating, per-pool disclosures, and price oracles tied to real-world exchanges, all implementable via Uniswap v4 hooks without modifying the core AMM. The exemption will run for five years and targets a $79 trillion US equities market, where AMM settlement is atomic and final compared to the T+1 cycle in traditional clearinghouses.

articles.title: IS HYPERLIQUID LOSING ITS LONG-TAIL LIQUIDITY MOAT?
articles.summary: Analysis of orderbook data from November 2025 to November 2026 across 38 comparable markets shows Hyperliquid's long-tail dollar depth fell 82%, versus 61% on Binance and 78% on OKX. After controlling for token price declines, the HL-to-Binance depth ratio dropped 57.5% at 5 bps, with $10k execution costs running 5.21 bps on HL versus 2.95 bps on Binance. Wintermute's monopolization of read priority fees and L1 congestion at 25-40k TPS have disadvantaged smaller market makers, pushing them to widen spreads and reduce depth in response to adverse selection risk. The deterioration threatens Hyperliquid's founding differentiation: deep liquidity in long-tail assets was the moat separating it from centralized venues.

articles.title: DEFI MOATS IN AN AI WORLD
articles.summary: AI tooling has collapsed the cost of launching DeFi products from six-month, $3M builds to weekend projects, but Multicoin Capital's Spencer Applebaum argues this commoditization strengthens incumbent protocol moats rather than eroding them. Financial moats, including liquidity depth, customer trust, and proprietary risk underwriting, require years to accumulate and sit beyond what AI can replicate from scratch. Multicoin's updated DeFi value-capture framework adds AI agents as the next class of sophisticated users, gravitating toward protocols with the deepest liquidity and most reliable execution at scale rather than those competing on software features or UI. This positions protocols like Uniswap, Aave, and Hyperliquid as primary beneficiaries as DEX market share against CEXs hits all-time highs and institutional adoption of tokenized assets accelerates.

articles.title: STOCK TOKENS ARE WHERE STABLECOINS WERE IN 2023
articles.summary: DTCC's new tokenization service is the biggest change in markets since paper certificates went away in the 1970s, yet will be mostly unused for a while. The market is tiny (about 0.004% of stocks and ETFs, with $4.6B of tokenized stocks, nearly all wrapped tokens backed by shares at one broker, Alpaca) and is similar to stablecoins in 2023, about 18 months before they took off. There are currently four models: wrapped (xStocks, no shareholder rights), pooled (OKXICE, where 56 of 62 targeted companies opted out), mirrored (DTCC, with 34 securities on Canton and Besu and one Canton transaction so far), and native (Superstate and Figure, which need SEC rule changes). A Warren-led Senate Banking Committee and faster settlement hurting netting are potential headwinds. Banks that sit out tokenization risk buying it later from Robinhood or BlackRock.

articles.title: BUILDING NETWORKS FOR AGENTS
articles.summary: The intents model used by protocols like UniswapX, where users sign outcome-specified orders and providers compete to fill them, offers a template for agent-to-agent commerce networks that handle complex multi-party preference matching across everyday goods and services. Exchanges that currently require excessive coordination overhead become tractable when each party's agent can programmatically bid and accept offers within pre-authorized limits. Founders building these networks face four concrete design problems: enabling agent discovery of relevant suppliers, verifying supplier performance, pricing preferences that are fuzzy and multidimensional, and preventing fake demand or supply on either side. Crypto and stablecoins serve as the natural settlement layer for machine-to-machine transactions in these markets.

articles.title: ANOTHER “BEST CRYPTO CARD EVER” IS A SCAM
articles.summary: A site claiming to offer a no-KYC, instant-approval card with up to 5% cashback, a $50K monthly limit, Apple and Google Pay, airport lounges, cashback in BTC, ETH, or stablecoins, and backing from a16z, Paradigm, Sequoia, Pantera, and Bitcoin Capital is a scam.
